Consider the relations \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) defined as aR1b⇔a2+b2=1 for all \(a, b \in R\) and (a,b)R2(c,d)⇔ a+d=b+c for all \(( a , b ),( c , d ) \in N \times N\). Then

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For \(R_1: a R_1 b \Longleftrightarrow a^2+b^2=1\).

Reflexive: \(a R_1 a \Longleftrightarrow 2 a^2=1\), which is not true for all \(a \in \mathbb{R}\).

So \(R_1\) is not reflexive, hence not an equivalence relation.

For \(R_2:(a, b) R_2(c, d) \Longleftrightarrow a+d=b+c \Longleftrightarrow a-b=c-d\).

Reflexive: \(a-b=a-b\), so true.

Symmetric: if \(a-b=c-d\), then \(c-d=a-b\), so true.

Transitive: if \(a-b=c-d\) and \(c-d=e-f\), then \(a-b=e-f\), so true.

questions.question:
Let \(f(x)=\left|2 x^2+5\right| x|-3|, x \in R\). If \(m\) and \(n\) denote the number of points where \(f\) is not continuous and not differentiable respectively, then \(m + n\) is equal to:

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Since \(2x^2+5>0\)

for every real \(x\),

\(|2x^2+5|=2x^2+5\)

Therefore,

\(f(x)=\left|(2x^2+5)|x|-3\right|\)

The functions \(x^2\), \(|x|\), and the outer absolute value are continuous. Hence, \(f\) is continuous for every real \(x\).

Thus, \(m=0\)

Put \(t=|x|\geq0\)

Since \(x^2=t^2\),

\((2x^2+5)|x|-3=2t^3+5t-3\)

At \(x=0\), this inner expression equals \(-3\)

For \(x\) sufficiently close to \(0\), it remains negative. Hence, near \(x=0\),

\(f(x)=3-5|x|-2|x|^3\)

Therefore, \(f'_+(0)=-5\) and \(f'_-(0)=5\)

Thus, \(f\) is not differentiable at \(x=0\).

Other points of non-differentiability can occur where \(2t^3+5t-3=0\)

because the outer absolute value creates a corner when its inner expression changes sign.

Let \(\phi(t)=2t^3+5t-3\), \(t\geq0\)

Then \(\phi(0)=-3\) and \(\phi(1)=2+5-3=4\)

Therefore, there is at least one root \(r\) in \((0,1)\)

Also, \(\phi'(t)=6t^2+5>0\) for every \(t\geq0\)

Hence, \(\phi(t)\) is strictly increasing and can have only one non-negative root.

Thus, there is exactly one positive root \(r\)

The equation \(|x|=r\) gives two points,

\(x=r\) and \(x=-r\)

At \(x=r\), the derivative of the inner expression is \(6r^2+5\ne0\)

At \(x=-r\), its derivative is \(-(6r^2+5)\ne0\)

Therefore, the inner expression changes sign at both points, and the outer absolute value produces a corner at each.

Hence, \(f\) is not differentiable at exactly three points:

\(-r,0,r\)

Thus, \(n=3\)

Therefore, \(m+n=0+3=3\)

The differential equation is
\(f'(x)=\alpha f(x)+3\)

Using \(f(0)=2\), we get
\(\Rightarrow C=2+\dfrac{3}{\alpha}\)
For \(\alpha>0\), \(e^{\alpha x}\to0\) as \(x\to-\infty\).
\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)=-\dfrac{3}{\alpha}\)

questions.question:
Let \(f:(0, \infty) \rightarrow R \) and \( F (x)=\int_0^x t f( t ) dt \). If \(F \left(x^2\right)=x^4+x^5 \) then \(\sum_{ r =1}^{12} f\left( r ^2\right) \) is equal to__________ 

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Since \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}t f(t)\,dt\), the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus gives \(F'(x)=x f(x)\).

Differentiate \(F(x^2)=x^4+x^5\) with respect to \(x\).

Then \(F'(x^2)\cdot2x=4x^3+5x^4\).

Using \(F'(x^2)=x^2f(x^2)\), we get \(2x^3f(x^2)=4x^3+5x^4\).

For \(x>0\), \(f(x^2)=2+\dfrac{5x}{2}\).

Therefore, \(f(r^2)=2+\dfrac{5r}{2}\).

Hence \(\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{12}f(r^2)=\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{12}\left(2+\dfrac{5r}{2}\right)=24+\dfrac{5}{2}\cdot\dfrac{12\cdot13}{2}=24+195=219\).

questions.question:
Three points \(O (0,0), P \left( a , a ^2\right), Q \left(- b , b ^2\right), a >0, b >0\), are on the parabola \(y=x^2\). Let \(S _1\) be the area of the region bounded by the line \(PQ\) and the parabola, and \(S _2\) be the area of the triangle \(OPQ\). If the minimum value of \(\frac{ S _1}{ S _2}\) is \(\frac{ m }{ n }, \operatorname{gcd}( m , n )=1\), then \(m + n\) is equal to____________.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The line through \(P(a,a^2)\) and \(Q(-b,b^2)\) is \(y=(a-b)x+ab\).

The difference between the line and the parabola is \((a-b)x+ab-x^2=(a-x)(x+b)\).

Therefore, \(S_1=\displaystyle\int_{-b}^{a}(a-x)(x+b)dx=\dfrac{(a+b)^3}{6}\).

The area of \(\triangle OPQ\) is \(S_2=\dfrac{1}{2}|a\cdot b^2-a^2(-b)|\).

Thus \(S_2=\dfrac{ab(a+b)}{2}\).

Hence \(\dfrac{S_1}{S_2}=\dfrac{(a+b)^2}{3ab}=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{b}{a}+2\right)\).

Since \(a>0\) and \(b>0\), \(\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{b}{a}\geq2\).

Therefore, \(\dfrac{S_1}{S_2}\geq\dfrac{4}{3}\), with equality when \(a=b\).

Thus the minimum value is \(\dfrac{m}{n}=\dfrac{4}{3}\).

Hence \(m+n=4+3=7\).

questions.question:
The sum of squares of all possible values of \(k\), for which area of the region bounded by the parabolas \(2 y^2= k x\) and \(k y^2=2(y-x)\) is maximum, is equal to__________

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The first parabola gives \(x=\dfrac{2y^2}{k}\).

The second parabola gives \(x=y-\dfrac{ky^2}{2}\).

Apart from the origin, their intersection satisfies \(\dfrac{2y^2}{k}=y-\dfrac{ky^2}{2}\).

Thus \(y=\dfrac{2k}{k^2+4}\).

The horizontal width of the enclosed region is \(y-\dfrac{ky^2}{2}-\dfrac{2y^2}{k}=y-\dfrac{k^2+4}{2k}y^2\).

Let \(c=\dfrac{k^2+4}{2k}\), so the non-zero intersection is \(y=\dfrac{1}{c}\).

Therefore, \(A=\left|\displaystyle\int_0^{1/c}(y-cy^2)dy\right|=\left|\left[\dfrac{y^2}{2}-\dfrac{cy^3}{3}\right]_0^{1/c}\right|=\dfrac{1}{6c^2}\).

Hence \(A=\dfrac{2k^2}{3(k^2+4)^2}\).

Let \(t=k^2\), where \(t>0\).

Then \(A=\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot\dfrac{t}{(t+4)^2}\).

Differentiating, \(\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{t}{(t+4)^2}\right)=\dfrac{4-t}{(t+4)^3}\).

Hence the area is maximum when \(t=4\), so \(k^2=4\).

Thus \(k=2\) or \(k=-2\).

The sum of the squares of all possible values is \(2^2+(-2)^2=8\).

Here \(P=-\frac{1}{y}\), so integrating factor \(=\mathrm{e}^{\int -\frac{1}{y}dy}=\frac{1}{y}\).

Multiplying by \( \frac{1}{y} \), we get

questions.question:
Let \(\overrightarrow{ a }=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \overrightarrow{ b }=-\hat{i}-8 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}\) and \(\overrightarrow{ c }=4 \hat{i}+ c _2 \hat{j}+ c _3 \hat{k}\) be three vectors such that \(\overrightarrow{ b } \times \overrightarrow{ a }=\overrightarrow{ c } \times \overrightarrow{ a }\). If the angle between the vector \(\overrightarrow{ c }\) and the vector \(3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+\hat{k}\) is \(\theta\), then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(\tan ^2 \theta\) is___________

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The condition \(\vec b\times\vec a=\vec c\times\vec a\) gives \((\vec b-\vec c)\times\vec a=\vec0\).

\(\vec b-\vec c=\lambda\vec a\)

\(\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\)

\(\vec b=-\hat i-8\hat j+2\hat k\)

\(\vec c=4\hat i+c_2\hat j+c_3\hat k\)

Comparing the \(\hat i\)-components in \(\vec b-\vec c=\lambda\vec a\), we get \(\lambda=-5\).

\(-8-c_2=-5\)

\(c_2=-3\)

\(2-c_3=-5\)

\(c_3=7\)

\(\vec c=4\hat i-3\hat j+7\hat k\)

Let \(\vec d=3\hat i+4\hat j+\hat k\).

\(\vec c\cdot\vec d=12-12+7=7\)

\(|\vec c|^2=16+9+49=74\)

\(|\vec d|^2=9+16+1=26\)

If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec c\) and \(\vec d\), then \(\tan^2\theta=\dfrac{|\vec c|^2|\vec d|^2-(\vec c\cdot\vec d)^2}{(\vec c\cdot\vec d)^2}\).

\(\tan^2\theta=\dfrac{74\times26-49}{49}=\dfrac{1875}{49}\)

\(38<\dfrac{1875}{49}<39\)

\(\left\lfloor\tan^2\theta\right\rfloor=38\)

\(\therefore\) the required value is \(38\)

questions.question:
Let \(ABC\) be an isosceles triangle in which \(A\) is at \((-1,0), \angle A =\frac{2 \pi}{3}, AB = AC\) and \(B\) is on the positive \(x\)-axis. If \(BC =4 \sqrt{3}\) and the line \(BC\) intersects the line \(y=x+3\) at \((\alpha, \beta)\), then \(\frac{\beta^4}{\alpha^2}\) is_________

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(B=(b,0)\), where \(b>0\).

\(AB=b+1\)

Since \(AB=AC\) and \(\angle A=120^\circ\), the cosine rule gives the following relation.

\(BC^2=AB^2+AC^2-2(AB)(AC)\cos120^\circ=3AB^2\)

\(4\sqrt3=\sqrt3\,AB\)

\(\Rightarrow AB=4\)

\(\Rightarrow B=(3,0)\)

Taking the position of \(C\) above the \(x\)-axis, \(C=(-3,2\sqrt3)\); the reflected position gives the same requested value.

The slope of \(BC\) is \(m\).

\(m=\dfrac{2\sqrt3-0}{-3-3}=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\)

The equation of \(BC\) is the following.

\(y=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}(x-3)\)

We impose the intersection condition \(y=x+3\).

\(x+3=\dfrac{3-x}{\sqrt3}\)

\(\Rightarrow \alpha=-6+3\sqrt3\)

\(\Rightarrow \beta=\alpha+3=-3+3\sqrt3\)

\(\beta^2=9(\sqrt3-1)^2=36-18\sqrt3\)

\(-6\alpha=-6(-6+3\sqrt3)=36-18\sqrt3\)

\(\Rightarrow \beta^2=-6\alpha\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\beta^4}{\alpha^2}=36\)

The final answer is \(36\).
